clue.text: One in business who has retired?

definitions.text: One in business who has retired?

parts.words: One in business who has retired?
parts.note: a backer who has gone to bed has 'retired', yet the investor in question merely takes no active part in running the firm

explanation.surface: A query about a business figure who has stepped back from work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' means gone to bed, so the person is literally asleep beside a business colleague; the real term is for a silent investor.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent investor puts money into a firm but takes no part in its management, much as one who is asleep does nothing.

clue.text: A new broom often makes them

definitions.text: A new broom often makes them

parts.words: A new broom often makes them
parts.note: the saying 'a new broom sweeps clean' describes a newcomer who overhauls everything, and a broom literally sweeps

explanation.surface: A household broom brushing the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'new broom' is a fresh manager keen on reform, and brooms also sweep.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesale reforms brought in by a newly appointed boss, playing on the proverb that a new broom sweeps clean.

clue.text: Once article for sale comes up, applaud

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at auction

explanation.surface: At an auction, once an item is offered, the room claps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns LOT into TOL beneath EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise highly; both words express warm approval of someone.

clue.text: Will find postal order in one's wallet

indicators.note: in places the order inside the wallet, so those letters go within

parts.note: a purse is a wallet for coins

explanation.surface: Someone finds a postal order tucked into their wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name or verb but is the noun meaning determination.
explanation.definitionFit: Will in the sense of resolve or intention: a firm aim or determination.

clue.text: Brief communication raising school rent

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising the school name means writing it upwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school
to let is to rent out a property

explanation.surface: A short note about a school putting up its rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raising' looks like an increase in rent; it turns ETON into NOTE. ETON is an English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folded sheet for a short letter; a brief written message.

clue.text: While away time in a sea journey

parts.note: to while away time is to pass it
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Killing time while on a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a voyage by ship, as in booking a passage to America.

clue.text: Conductor's support for uplifting alternative string sound

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting the word up writes it backwards

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a strum is the sound of strings brushed on a guitar

explanation.surface: An orchestral conductor seeking an uplifting alternative sound from the strings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' seems to praise the music; it turns OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised platform on which a conductor stands is a podium, physically supporting them.

clue.text: A bloomer he made, being too fond of his image

definitions.text: A bloomer he made, being too fond of his image

parts.words: A bloomer he made, being too fond of his image
parts.note: in Greek myth the youth fell for his own reflection and was changed into a flower; a bloomer is both a flower and a blunder

explanation.surface: Someone made a blunder through vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' reads as a mistake, but it is also a flowering plant, which this vain youth became.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical youth who loved his reflection gave his name to the daffodil family of flowers.

clue.text: Takes part in a hit parade

definitions.text: Takes part in a hit parade

parts.words: Takes part in a hit parade
parts.note: a hit parade sounds like a pop chart, but here it is a line of people striking someone who passes between them

explanation.surface: A musician appearing in the pop charts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit parade' is a music chart; read literally it is two rows of people beating whoever runs between them, an old military punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Running between two lines of attackers was a punishment; the phrase now means facing a barrage of criticism.

clue.text: To begin with, it is an internal inflammation

parts.note: to enter on something is to begin it

explanation.surface: An opening remark introducing a medical condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To begin with' looks like a phrase meaning firstly; 'To begin' gives ENTER and 'with' just joins it to IT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the intestine, an organ inside the body, often from infection.

clue.text: Warning! This woman is dangerous

definitions.meaning: a loud wailing alarm, as on a police car
a seductive temptress, after the mythical singers who lured sailors to wreck

explanation.surface: A cautionary shout about a hazardous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an alarm signal and an alluring woman who leads men to ruin, from Greek myth.

clue.text: Handy lubricant?

parts.note: oiling a palm, the hand's inner surface, means bribing someone to make things run smoothly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy' means convenient, but here it means of the hand: greasing a palm is bribery. Literally it is also a tropical vegetable oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a vegetable oil; figuratively a bribe that smooths the way, from the idiom of greasing someone's palm.

clue.text: If trail is vandalised, supplies by plane

indicators.note: something vandalised is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: If a path is wrecked, goods have to be flown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is vandalised' rearranges IF TRAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport goods or people by aircraft, especially in an emergency.

clue.text: Form of food produced in layers

definitions.text: Form of food produced in layers

parts.words: Form of food produced in layers
parts.note: layers suggests strata like a lasagne, but here layers are hens

explanation.surface: Food made in stacked strata, such as a layered pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like strata; it means laying hens, which produce this food.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens bred for laying are called layers, and they produce this breakfast food.

clue.text: Certainly it's not Far Eastern in origin

indicators.note: the word Eastern is reworked into its source form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on something whose roots are not in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far Eastern' reads as a phrase, but 'Far' ends the definition and 'Eastern' is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of close: whatever is closest is certainly not far away.

clue.text: Does this imply sharecropping?

parts.note: sharecropping is tenant farming for a share of the crop; here the share is a plot of ground for growing vegetables

explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a rented garden plot in Britain; the word also means a share handed out, so cropping a share fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A small plot rented for growing vegetables; also a portion allocated, hence a share to crop.

clue.text: Appeal of love on board ship

indicators.note: on board places it within the vessel, inside its letters

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A romantic plea made aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' puts O inside SS.
explanation.definitionFit: The international distress signal is a desperate call for help.

clue.text: All together in France

parts.note: the phrase meaning all together is French, so it is what the French would say

explanation.surface: Everyone gathered as one somewhere in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase used in English meaning as a whole group, everyone at once.

clue.text: Born and even briefly raised

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means read from the bottom up
the poetic shortening of the word even drops its V, as in e'en

explanation.surface: Someone born and brought up as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens EVEN to the poetic E'EN, and 'raised' turns EEN round.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before a married woman's maiden name, it is French for born.

clue.text: Firm has a deficit — one in large figures

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a loss is a financial deficit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company running at a loss, one of the big players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large figures' seems financial, but means giant statues.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge statues such as the one at Rhodes; giant sculpted figures.

clue.text: Possibly train as a singer

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone could train to be a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TRAIN AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank, the American crooner, is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Post one is after is one in a Shiite sect

indicators.note: after places the mail and one later in the entry, following the is

parts.note: mail is the post
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A letter being chased by a member of a religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'is after' as chasing; it is the charade signal, putting the first 'is' at the front of the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a branch of Shia Islam led by the Aga Khan.

clue.text: There's no catch in it

parts.note: no catch suggests no hidden snag, but here it means no fish can be caught there

explanation.walkthrough: 'no catch' sounds like a deal with no snag; it means no fish, since this salt lake is too salty for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake between Israel and Jordan is too briny for fish to live, so anglers catch nothing.

clue.text: Breathless piper lacks expression

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for an expressionless face or manner

parts.note: one who no longer breathes is dead
Pan is the pipe-playing Greek god

explanation.surface: A piper out of breath can no longer play expressively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathless' suggests being winded, not dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a blank, impassive face that shows no feeling or emotion.

clue.text: A number leave one country for another

indicators.note: leave means these letters depart from the country's name

parts.note: Australia is a country
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Emigrants leaving one country for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like a crowd of people but gives A and L (fifty); 'leave' removes them from AUSTRALIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpine republic is simply another country, as the clue's second nation.

clue.text: She means to seek legal redress

definitions.meaning: a common girl's name, standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman intends to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a girl's name and the verb for taking a lawsuit against someone.

clue.text: Many not able to provide a word of opposite meaning

indicators.note: the words are able to provide another word when their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Plenty of people cannot come up with an opposite word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'able to provide' rearranges MANY NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot and cold are examples of words with contrary senses.

clue.text: Refrain from giving sailor a dirty look

parts.note: AB stands for able seaman
a stain is a dirty mark that spoils the look of something

explanation.surface: Not giving a seaman a scornful glare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a dirty look' seems to be a glare, but here it is a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold back from doing something, as from voting or drinking.

clue.text: Tina set up with a new name

indicators.note: in a down entry, set up means written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Tina is given a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns TINA into ANIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, unrelated to the others in the clue, hence a fresh one.

clue.text: Hail or drops of water in Scotland

definitions.meaning: in Scots the word means to weep, shedding teardrops

explanation.surface: Hailstones or rain in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hail' seems to be weather beside water drops, but it means welcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Welcome someone; also the Scots verb to weep, shedding tears.

clue.text: Just not taking sides

explanation.definitionFit: Both fair-minded and neutral describe a judge who favours neither party.

clue.text: Post-free?

parts.note: post-free suggests no postage to pay, but here a post is a job that is free, unfilled

explanation.walkthrough: 'Post-free' suggests free postage; it means a job going spare, as in a job advertisement heading.
explanation.definitionFit: The heading for a job advertisement: a position that is open and unfilled.
